candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record specifies a fat-signal mass arising from the interatrial septum (lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum on TTE; lentiform fat mass between aorta and SVC on MRI) causing SVC narrowing and hemodynamic compression. C001 labels it as a 'cardiac lipoma of the superior vena cava,' which captures the lipomatous nature and SVC involvement but misattributes the anatomic origin to the SVC itself rather than the interatrial septum, and does not explicitly name the SVC compression as the pathophysiologic consequence. The reference diagnosis requires both the interatrial septal origin and the SVC compression component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies a cardiac lipoma involving the SVC but omits the interatrial septal origin and the resulting SVC compression as a composite diagnostic component

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis combines anatomic origin (interatrial septum) with hemodynamic consequence (SVC compression); candidates should address both components for complete equivalence
Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum vs. true lipoma distinction is clinically relevant but not disambiguated in the record
